MEETINGS ON ZOOM, BY PHONE AND ON YOUTUBE
Meetings are recorded and are archived on the Town’s
YouTube Channel
for later viewing.
Members of the Public who wish to participate in the meeting may do so by visiting either of the following options:
1)
Zoom Video Links are included on each Agenda
, as they change each week.
•
Find Selectboard Agendas here.
•
Find a listing of recently posted documents here.
2) In the event that we are unable to provide real-time access to these meetings through technological means, despite best efforts, we will post on the Town of Blandford website a transcript or other comprehensive record of proceedings as soon as possible after the meeting as described in the provisions of the Open Meeting Law.
Emergency Alert System
Sign up for our Emergency Alert Notification System to receive official town updates pertaining to emergencies, town news, traffic hazards, fire, police, maintenance, and more.
Please note that this link will open in a new window

Tuesdays:
6-8pm
Saturdays:
8am-12pm
SWAP SHACK
The Swap Shack is meant to serve as a recycle & reuse center for Blandford residents who have a transfer station sticker.
For details on what is and is not accepted, download the flyer.
DONATE CLOTHING & SHOES HERE
Residents are now able to donate clothing and shoes at our Transfer Station. Each pound of clothing donated helps Blandford!
More details here.
•
See Transfer Station Rules & Regs here (updated 4/2021).
•
View the Fee Schedule here.
Visit the Board of Health page for more Transfer Station information →
Use of Town Hall Gym
The use of Town Hall gym is for recreation and events open to the public only and not for private use.
Residents and Town Officials interested in scheduling the gym for events and recreational use open for the public should call
(413) 848-4279
, ext. 206.
Tree Concerns?
Tree related issues should be directed to Mark Boomsma, Tree Warden, at
(413) 717-0212
.

About Blandford
The first settlers arrived in what is now Blandford in 1735. They were Scots-Irish coming from Hopkinton, Massachusetts (30 miles from Boston). In keeping with their Scottish heritage, they chose Glasgow as the name for the new settlement.
